name: Marine / boatyard / marina management
hypothesis: Dockwa is bookings; ops side (work orders, slip mgmt, haulouts, parts) weak.

market_sizing.target_buyer: Marina general manager or owner of a commercial marina, boatyard, or yacht club. Often a single decision-maker who also runs the workshop and reports to a board (yacht club) or owner-operator (private marina).
market_sizing.business_count_au: ~291-296 commercial marinas, yacht clubs and boatyards in AU (Marina Industries Association data via Marine Business News 2024 and AIMS Marine Index 2025). MIA membership covers ~85% of major marinas and ~80% of facilities with 100+ berths. Realistic SaaS-serviceable count: ~250-280.
market_sizing.business_count_global: Global ~10,000-12,000 marinas/boatyards: US ~12,000 marinas (~1,200 with 100+ slips); UK ~500; CA ~600; EU ~5,000+. Molo claims customers in 47 US states + 10 countries.
market_sizing.typical_size: 50-500 berths/dry-stack spaces, 5-40 staff, A$2M-A$30M annual revenue. Mix of berthing income, fuel, haulout/yard fees, retail, and service workshop revenue.

pricing_reality.incumbent_pricing: All quote-only. PacsoftNG, DockMaster, Molo (Storable Marine), Dockwa, MarinaOffice, Harbour Assist, HarbaMaster, YouNav, Smart Waters — none publish public pricing. Industry estimates: A$300-A$2,000+/mo per marina depending on berths, modules, payments take rate. Dockwa monetises primarily via transient-booking commission (~3-5% of transient bookings).
pricing_reality.willingness_to_pay: AU realistic ACV A$350-A$900/mo per small-to-mid marina; A$1,500+/mo for 200+ berth facilities. Top of $100-500 band realistic only for the smallest yacht clubs / single-boatyard operators. Mid-tier is genuinely $500-$2,000/mo territory — meaning this vertical exceeds the brief's price band for the median buyer.
pricing_reality.sales_motion: Outside sales / relationship-driven. MIA conference + on-site demos required for facilities >100 berths. Inside sales viable for smaller yacht clubs and single boatyards. Long sales cycle (3-9 months).
pricing_reality.expansion_revenue_potential: Strong: payments rake on berth + transient + workshop invoices (significant GMV per marina), fuel-dock POS, smart-meter electricity/water reconciliation (YouNav model), transient marketplace commission (Dockwa model), workshop parts marketplace, insurance referral. 2-3x ARPU lift very plausible via payments alone given high-ticket marine invoices.

competitive_landscape.incumbents: 1) PacsoftNG (NZ-based, acquired by Jonas Software 2018, 20+ years) — dominant ANZ marina platform; 2) DockMaster (US, owned by Valsoft) — legacy US incumbent with marina + boatyard + dealership modules; 3) Molo / Storable Marine (US, part of Storable storage-platform consolidator) — modern SaaS, 47 US states; 4) Dockwa (US, raised $13M+, owned by Marinas.com) — bookings-first, weak ops; 5) Harbour Assist (UK) — cloud, growing; 6) MarinaOffice, Total Marina Package, HarbaMaster, YouNav, Smart Waters, M-PRO — mid-tier and niche. In AU, PacsoftNG is the de-facto incumbent; Dockwa has limited AU traction.
competitive_landscape.incumbent_age_years: PacsoftNG ~20+ years (well into UI-rot territory); DockMaster ~25+ years (heavy UI rot documented); Molo ~10 years (modern); Dockwa ~10 years.
competitive_landscape.user_satisfaction_signals: DockMaster reviews (Capterra/G2/SoftwareAdvice): 'extremely outdated UI', 'clunky not intuitive', 'feels old', 'reporting requires unique naming conventions', 'cannot delete items - everything is reverse + rekey', 'cannot edit invoice once saved', 'every update breaks something next day'. PacsoftNG: reviews more favourable on support, but UI dated. Marina operators on industry forums complain bookings (Dockwa) is separate from ops (Pacsoft/DockMaster) — no unified system. Boatyard work-order side specifically weak across all incumbents; many shops run QuickBooks + Excel + paper job cards alongside the marina system.
competitive_landscape.recent_funding_or_ma: Storable acquired Molo (date pre-2023); Jonas Software owns Pacsoft (acquired 2018); Valsoft owns DockMaster; Dockwa acquired by Marinas.com 2022. Pattern: roll-up by vertical-SaaS holding companies (Jonas, Constellation, Valsoft, Volaris), not VC growth funding. Few net-new entrants since ~2020 in the boatyard ops segment.
competitive_landscape.ai_disruption_risk: Low. No identified AI-native marina/boatyard SaaS raising rounds as of mid-2026. AI-assisted scheduling and predictive haulout demand are obvious adjacent features but no challenger has staked the wedge. Window relatively open.

opportunity_quality.core_pain: Marinas with workshops run a fragmented stack: PacsoftNG/DockMaster for berths + invoicing, Dockwa for transient bookings, paper or Excel for haulout schedule + yard map, QuickBooks/Xero for accounts, and separate workshop software (or paper) for work orders + parts + labour. Sublease/work-on-vessel insurance, marine-trade contractor sign-in, and tide-aware haulout scheduling are entirely manual. Parts inventory for stern-drive/outboard/rigging is tracked in Excel. Hypothesis check confirmed: Dockwa is bookings; ops side (work orders, slip mgmt, haulouts, parts) is weak across incumbents.
opportunity_quality.moat_source: Integration moat: PacsoftNG/DockMaster data import + payments. Workflow moat: tide-aware haulout schedule + yard map + work order + parts in one system. Network effect via cross-marina transient traveller (Dockwa model) is the largest available moat but requires consumer side. AU regulatory moat is weak (no APVMA equivalent).
opportunity_quality.critical_integrations: Xero / MYOB (mandatory in AU); Stripe + Tyro EFTPOS; smart meters (electricity/water sub-metering — Yo-Smart, EziMeter); fuel POS; tide data (BOM); AIS vessel-tracking feeds; Dockwa / Marinas.com inbound transient bookings; insurance certificate verification; MIA/Global Marina Institute training certificates.
opportunity_quality.incumbent_ehr_lock_in: Moderate. PacsoftNG/DockMaster own years of berthing + customer history. Side-car play (bolt onto Pacsoft, replace workshop module first) more realistic than rip-and-replace for established marinas. Fresh boatyards and yacht clubs are greenfield.

build_difficulty.regulatory_complexity: Moderate. MARPOL waste tracking, AMSA vessel registration (federal), state Marine Safety Acts, port authority lease conditions, biosecurity (DAFF) for international transients, OH&S for hot-work on vessels (welding/grinding permits), insurance certificate compliance for contractors entering the yard.
build_difficulty.regulatory_changes_2025_2026: No identified single forcing function. Background: AMSA Domestic Commercial Vessel National Law continues phased rollout; biosecurity vessel inspection rules tightening post-2023; some states (NSW Maritime, Marine Safety VIC) modernising commercial-marina permit conditions. Insurance / WHS pressure on contractor sign-in is the most consistent operational forcing function but is industry-driven not regulator-driven.
build_difficulty.domain_depth: High. Marinas have idiosyncratic workflows: tide tables, dry-stack rack assignments, slip dimensions vs vessel LOA + beam + draft, transient turnover, fuel-dock reconciliation, haulout sling capacity scheduling. Outsider needs 6+ months and 2-3 design-partner marinas to ship credible MVP.
build_difficulty.mvp_effort: 8-12 months for solo/small team. Berth/slip allocation engine + haulout schedule + work order + parts + payments + Xero is materially more code than mobile mechanic or pest control MVPs.
build_difficulty.technical_risks: Slip-to-vessel assignment optimisation (LOA + beam + draft + power + sun/wind preference); haulout sling-capacity scheduling with tide windows; offline-tolerant mobile for dock staff; integration with smart utility meters (heterogeneous protocols); migration from legacy PacsoftNG/DockMaster databases.
build_difficulty.state_by_state_variance_au: Low. Marine safety and biosecurity differ by state but core workflow portable. Lease conditions vary marina to marina more than state to state.
build_difficulty.data_residency_requirement: Soft. AU hosting preferred by government-owned marinas (port authorities, councils). Not legally mandated for private operators.

distribution_difficulty.channel_options: 1) MIA annual conference + state events — central go-to-market channel (most AU buyers attend); 2) Global Marina Institute certified-marina-manager network; 3) Marine Business News, Marine Industry News, MySailing publications; 4) AIMEX (Australian Marine Export Group) for boatyard segment; 5) Direct outbound — MIA member list is partially public, ~250 reachable buyers total (entire AU TAM fits in a CRM); 6) Boat shows (Sydney International Boat Show, Sanctuary Cove) — premium booth but visibility to marina ops staff is incidental.
distribution_difficulty.trade_association_count_au: ~4 (MIA, AIMEX, BIA NSW/state boating industry associations, Yachting Australia/Australian Sailing). Tight, well-organised.
distribution_difficulty.trade_publication_count: ~3-5 (Marine Business News, Marine Industry News, MySailing, Modern Boating, Multihull World).
distribution_difficulty.industry_facebook_group_size: Small. Marina operations is not a Facebook-group-led community; LinkedIn is dominant. Estimated <5,000 across operator groups.
distribution_difficulty.conference_event_count_au: 2-3 (MIA Annual Conference, Sanctuary Cove International Boat Show, Sydney International Boat Show — but only MIA reaches marina operators specifically). Under-$10K booth at MIA realistic.
distribution_difficulty.cold_outbound_viability: Very high. The entire AU TAM is ~290 named facilities, listed in MIA directory, MyMarinaGuide, and Superyacht Services Guide. Phone + email of GMs publicly available. Account-based marketing is the natural motion.
distribution_difficulty.founder_market_fit_proxy: Moderate-low. Marina GMs are conservative buyers; trust insiders (ex-marina-manager co-founder or advisor strongly preferred). Industry is small, reputation travels fast — first 3 customers gate the next 20.
distribution_difficulty.case_study_acquisition_cost: High. 5 reference customers in 6-12 months realistic with persistent ABM + MIA conference attendance + ex-industry advisor. Each design partner is a high-touch 3-month onboarding.
distribution_difficulty.content_seo_competitiveness: Low. 'Marina management software Australia', 'PacsoftNG alternative', 'DockMaster alternative' have low DR competitors. SEO matters less than ABM for a 290-buyer TAM.
distribution_difficulty.insurer_or_gatekeeper_dependency: Low for core product. Contractor insurance verification is workflow not gatekept API. Dockwa transient feed is desirable but not blocking — competitors exist (Snag-A-Slip).

personal_fit.manuva_data_model_reuse_pct: 45-60%. Direct reuse: tenant + RLS, auth, customers (= berth holders + vessel owners), suppliers (= chandlery + parts), inventory items + bins (= chandlery store + workshop parts bins), purchase orders, activity_log, production orders re-skinned as work orders, BOM re-skinned as service kits. New: vessels (with LOA/beam/draft/power), berths/slips (with dimensions + utilities), haulout schedule, tide-aware allocation engine, smart-meter integration, transient bookings.
personal_fit.manuva_code_reuse: Auth, tenant context, RLS, server actions, activity logging, Xero/MYOB scaffold, design system, inventory + bin model, production-order workflow — all transfer. BOM concept maps onto service kits (annual antifoul + zincs + service).
personal_fit.buyer_persona_overlap_with_manuva: Very low. AU manufacturers and marina GMs are disjoint markets. No bundle/expansion path. Fresh GTM.
personal_fit.adjacency_to_manufacturing: Low-moderate. Boatyards do contain a manufacturing-adjacent workshop (parts + labour + work orders), so Manuva's production-order + BOM + inventory muscle is genuinely reusable for the workshop module — but the marina-side (berths, haulouts, transient bookings) is foreign territory.
personal_fit.technical_moat_durability_months: 12-18 months. The slip/haulout allocation engine + tide integration + smart-meter integration + multi-incumbent data migration is genuinely hard. AI coding tools accelerate the CRUD but not the domain integration.

unit_economics.gross_margin_sensitivity: Healthy. Some payments-processing pass-through; smart-meter integrations are one-off; minimal AI inference required. Expect 80-85% gross margin. Outside-sales motion is the bigger margin pressure (CAC > unit cost).
unit_economics.multi_location_natural: Limited. Most marina operators run a single facility; a few groups operate 3-10 marinas (e.g. d'Albora Marinas, Superior Jetties customers). Per-marina pricing is the natural expansion lever; per-berth pricing also viable.
unit_economics.churn_risk: Low. Mission-critical operations system with high switching cost (years of berthing + financial history). Annual churn likely <8% once past year one. Long sales cycle balanced by long retention.
unit_economics.customers_needed_for_target_arr: ~130-150 customers at A$650 ARPU to hit A$1M ARR — but AU TAM of ~290 means ~50% market share required, making AU-only a sub-$1M ARR business. International expansion (NZ, UK, Pacific) mandatory for venture-scale outcomes.
